The Papists are never a whit better, save only that they sprinkle their satisfactions with the blood of Christ; but they deal too disorderly therein,
“Sed in eo nimio sunt praeposteri,” but in this they are exceedingly preposterous.
because, being not content with Christ alone, they gather to themselves, on every side, a thousand manner of sacrifices or satisfactions. Therefore, whosoever desireth to have remission of sins, let him not turn aside from Christ, even the least nail’s breadth.
When as we hear, that we have remission of sins by believing, we must understand and know the force and nature of faith, as undoubtedly Peter intreated abundantly of this, [viz.] after what sort we must believe in Christ. And this is nothing else, but with the sincere affection of the mind to embrace him as he is set before us in the gospel; so that faith dependeth upon the promises. Yet Peter seemeth to deal amiss, because whereas we have two principal things by our Savior Christ, he doth only make mention of the one of them; for he speaketh nothing of repentance and newness of 1ife, which ought not to be omitted in the sum of the gospel.
“Quae in evangelii summa praetermitti minime debuerat,” which ought by no means to have been omitted in a summary of the gospel.
But we may easily answer, That the regeneration of the Spirit is comprehended under faith, as it is an effect thereof. For we believe in Christ for this cause, partly that he may restore us unto the Father’s favor by the free imputation of righteousness; partly that he may sanctify us by his Spirit, And we know that we are adopted by God to be his children upon this condition, that he may govern us by his Spirit. Therefore, it was sufficient for Peter to show how men, who were by nature estranged from God, do return into favor with him.
As touching the third member, we need not reckon up all places of the prophets, where they set before us Christ to be the mediator, who by obtaining pardon for our sins, doth reconcile God to us; but this is their common order of teaching, and, as it were, their rule, to call back all the godly unto that covenant which God made with Abraham putting the mediator between.
“Mediatore interposito,” by the imposition of a Mediator.
Furthermore, this point is very needful to be known, that the grace which was offered at length by Christ is the same which the law and the prophets, in times past, delivered unto the fathers to be hoped for. And surely it was of great force with Cornelius and such like, who did greatly reverence the law and prophets, that they might know that that was performed and accomplished in very deed in Christ which was testified in the oracles of the prophets. Therefore, to the end the ministers of the Church may agree with the prophets in their form of teaching, let them study by preaching to set forth Christ; let them continually testify that we must seek righteousness at his hands alone, which consisteth upon [of] free remission of sins. This is another manner of antiquity than that which is showed with great boasting of the Papists, whilst that they thrust in the rotten inventions
“Putida... figmenta,” the foul figments.
of their satisfactions into the place of Christ’s blood.
Acts 10:44-48
44. And as Peter yet spake these words, the Spirit came down upon all which heard the word. 45. And they of the circumcision which believed were astonished, as many as came with Peter, because that on the Gentiles also were poured out the gifts of the Holy Ghost. 46. For they heard them speak with tongues, and glorify God. Then Peter answered, 47. Can any man forbid water, that these should not be baptized, who have received the Spirit as well as we? 48. And he commanded them to be baptized in the name of the Lord. Then prayed they him to tarry certain days.
entries.88fd6aab9ecfc5158e25b5c5b93b2670461a9b1c: <div annotateRef="Bible:Acts.10.44" annotateType="commentary" osisID="Acts.10.44" sID="gen109854" type="section"/> <div sID="gen109855" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">44.</hi> <hi type="italic">And as Peter yet spake.</hi> God declareth now by a new miracle, that the doctrine of the gospel is common as well to the Gentiles as to the Jews. And this is an excellent seal of the calling of the Gentiles; because the Lord would never have vouchsafed to bestow upon the Gentiles the graces of his Spirit, unless it had been to declare that even they were adopted together into the society of the covenant. These gifts, mentioned by Luke, differ indeed from the grace of regeneration; and yet, undoubtedly, God did by this means seal both Peter’s doctrine, and also their faith and godliness which heard him. He saith that they were <hi type="italic">all</hi> endowed with the Spirit, like as we saw before, that they came all encouraged to learn and obey.<div eID="gen109855" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen109856" type="x-p"/>This visible sign representeth unto us, as it were in a table, what an effectual instrument of God’s power the preaching of the gospel is; for he poured out his Spirit as Peter spake, to the end he might show that he sendeth not teachers to that end, that they may beat the air with the vain sound of their voice, but that he may work mightily by their voice, and may quicken the same by the power of his Spirit, to the salvation of the godly. Thus doth Paul put the Galatians (<reference osisRef="Bible:Gal.3.2">Galatians 3:2</reference>.) in mind, that they received the Holy Ghost by the hearing of faith; and in another place he saith that he is the minister of the Spirit, and not of the letter, (<reference osisRef="Bible:2Cor.3.6">2 Corinthians 3:6</reference>.) The gift of the tongues, and other such like things, are ceased long ago in the Church; but the spirit of understanding and of regeneration is of force, and shall always be of force, which the Lord coupleth with the external preaching of the gospel, that he may keep us in reverence of his word, and may prevent the deadly dotings, wherein brain-sick fellows enwrap themselves, whilst that, forsaking the word, they invent an erroneous and wandering spirit. But it doth not, nor shall not, always so fall out, that all those which hear the word with their outward ears, do or shall also receive the Spirit; and the ministers do seldom light upon such hearers as Peter had, who are willing, with one consent, to follow God. Yet he bringeth to pass that all the elect feel in themselves the consent of the external word, and of the secret power of the Spirit.<div eID="gen109856" type="x-p"/> <div annotateRef="Bible:Acts.10.44" annotateType="commentary" eID="gen109854" osisID="Acts.10.44" type="section"/>
entries.25e3d87c652c4482a10c28aac1fd6d31c56a4670: <div annotateRef="Bible:Acts.10.45" annotateType="commentary" osisID="Acts.10.45" sID="gen109857" type="section"/> <div sID="gen109858" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">45.</hi> <hi type="italic">The faithful were astonished.</hi> He calleth them faithful who were as yet possessed with a wicked error. So the Lord doth not by and by wipe away all clouds of ignorance from his, and yet they do not darken the praise of faith before God, because he pardoneth errors and doth vouchsafe to favor it, as if it were pure and plain. And yet it is a wonder, that seeing they knew that Peter was sent of God, they would now be amazed, as at some strange and new thing, because God giveth the grace of his Spirit to those to whom he would have Christ now preached; but the sudden change is the cause of this, because, whereas God until that day had separated the Gentiles from his people as strangers and aliens, he doth now favor them both alike, and lifteth them up into the like degree of honor. Although we be also taught by this example, how hard a matter it is for us to wind out ourselves out of our errors once conceived, especially when they are of any continuance.<div eID="gen109858" type="x-p"/> <div annotateRef="Bible:Acts.10.45" annotateType="commentary" eID="gen109857" osisID="Acts.10.45" type="section"/>
entries.919647652e293501f7f4bb9930cb66ba2aa73266: <div annotateRef="Bible:Acts.10.46" annotateType="commentary" osisID="Acts.10.46" sID="gen109859" type="section"/> <div sID="gen109860" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">46.</hi><hi type="italic"> For they heard them.</hi> He expresseth what gifts of the Spirit were poured out upon them, and therewithal he noteth the use; to wit, that they had variety of tongues given them, so that they did glorify God with many tongues. Also, it may be gathered out of this place, that the tongues were given them not only for necessity, seeing the gospel was to be preached to strangers and to men of another language, but also to be an ornament and worship to the gospel. But ambition did afterward corrupt this second use, forasmuch as many did translate that unto pomp and vain glory which they had received to set forth the dignity of the heavenly wisdom, as Paul doth sharply reprove this fault in the Corinthians. Therefore, no marvel if God took away that shortly after which he had given, and did not suffer the same to be corrupted with longer abuse.<div eID="gen109860" type="x-p"/> <div annotateRef="Bible:Acts.10.46" annotateType="commentary" eID="gen109859" osisID="Acts.10.46" type="section"/>
entries.9a7f016c6fe941f6c7f1a3cbdc41a3ec3fc37b4c: <div annotateRef="Bible:Acts.10.47" annotateType="commentary" osisID="Acts.10.47" sID="gen109861" type="section"/> <div sID="gen109862" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">47.</hi><hi type="italic"> Peter answered.</hi> Peter reasoneth from the thing to the sign; for, seeing that baptism is an addition or appurtenance of the spiritual grace, he which hath received the Spirit is also apt [fit] to receive baptism; and this is the (most) lawful order, that the minister admit those unto the receiving of the outward sign whom God hath testified to be his children by the mark and pledge of his Spirit; so that faith and doctrine are first. And whereas unlearned men infer thereupon that infants are not to be baptized, it is without all reason. I grant that those who are strangers from the Church must be taught before the sign of adoption be given them; but I say, that the children of the faithful which are born in the Church are from their mother’s womb of the household of the kingdom of God. Yea, the argument which they use preposterously against us do I turn back [retort] upon themselves; for, seeing that God hath adopted the children of the faithful before they be born, I conclude thereupon that they are not to be defrauded of the outward sign; otherwise men shall presume to take that from them which God hath granted them. As touching the manifest grace of the Spirit, there is no absurdity therein, if <note n="720"> <div sID="gen109863" type="x-p"/> “<foreign xml:lang="la">Tempore</foreign>,” in point of time.<div eID="gen109863" type="x-p"/> </note> it follow after baptism in them.<div eID="gen109862" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen109864" type="x-p"/>And as this testimony maketh nothing for maintenance of their error, so it doth strongly refute the error of the Papists, who tie the grace of the Spirit to the signs, and think that the same is fet [fetched] from heaven with enchantments, <note n="721"> <div sID="gen109865" type="x-p"/> “<foreign xml:lang="la">Eamque exorcismis non secus elici putant e coelo</foreign>,” and think it can only be brought down from heaven by exorcisms.<div eID="gen109865" type="x-p"/> </note> as those witches did think that they did pull down the moon with their charms. But forasmuch as Luke saith that these had the Holy Ghost given them who were not as yet baptized, he showeth that the Spirit is not included in baptism. Lastly, we must note that the apostles were content with water alone when as they did baptize, <note n="722"> <div sID="gen109866" type="x-p"/> “<foreign xml:lang="la">Ad conferendum baptismum</foreign>,” in giving baptism.<div eID="gen109866" type="x-p"/> </note> and would to God this plainness had been retained amongst their posterity, and that they had not gathered here and there divers trifles, whereof baptism is filth in Popery. They think that the worthiness of baptism is adorned with oil, salt, spittle, wax-candles, whereas they are rather filthy pollutions which corrupt the pure and natural [genuine] institution of Christ.<div eID="gen109864" type="x-p"/> <div annotateRef="Bible:Acts.10.47" annotateType="commentary" eID="gen109861" osisID="Acts.10.47" type="section"/>
entries.de77be20af993b54e017fa31eae3eff39dd5d8d6:
48. And he commanded them to be baptized. It was not of necessity that baptism should be ministered by Peter’s hand, as Paul doth likewise testify that he baptized few at Corinth, for other ministers might take this charge upon them. Whereas he saith, in the name of the Lord, it must not be restrained unto the form, as we have said in the third chapter; but because Christ is the proper scope of baptism, therefore are we said to be baptized in his name. When as Luke saith, last of all, that Peter was requested by Cornelius and his kinsmen that he would tarry a few days, he commendeth in them their desire to profit. They were, indeed, endued with the Holy Ghost; but they were not so come to the top, but that confirmation was as yet profitable for them. And, according to their example, so often as opportunity to profit offereth itself, we must use it diligently; and let us not swell with pride, which stoppeth the way before doctrine.
“Qui ingressum obstruat doctrinae,” which obstructeth the entrance of doctrine.
CHAPTER 11
Acts 11:1-18
1. And the apostles and brethren which were in Judea heard that the Gentiles also had embraced the word of God. 2. And when Peter was gone up to Jerusalem, those which were of the circumcision reasoned with him, 3. Saying, Thou wentest in unto men uncircumcised, and hast eaten with them. 4. And Peter began, and expounded to them in order, saying, 5. I was in the city Joppa praying; and being in a trance, I saw a vision, to wit, A certain vessel coming down from heaven like a great sheet, tied by the four corners, which came even unto me: 6. Which, when I considered earnestly, I saw then four-footed beasts of the earth, and wild beasts, and creeping things, and birds of the heaven. 7. And I heard a voice saying to me, Arise, Peter; slay and eat. 8. Then I said, Not so, Lord: Because there never entered into my mouth any common or unclean thing. 9. And the voice answered me the second time from heaven, Profane not thou those things which God hath made clean. 10. And this was done thrice: and they were all received into heaven again. 11. And, behold, the same hour three men stood nigh the house wherein I sat, being sent unto me from Cesarea. 12. And the Spirit commanded me to go with them, doubting nothing. And they came with me, and these six brethren, and we entered the man’s house. 13. And he told us how he had seen an angel standing at his house, and saying to him, Send men to Joppa, and fetch Simon, whose surname is Peter; 14. Who shall speak to thee words, whereby thou and all thy house shall be saved. 15. Furthermore, when I began to speak, the Holy Ghost fell down upon them, even as upon us at the beginning. 16. And I remembered the word of the Lord, how he had said, John truly hath baptized with water, but you shall be baptized with the Holy Ghost. 17. Therefore, seeing that God had given them the like gift as unto us, which was believed in the Lord Jesus Christ, who was I that could let [hinder] God? 18. When they had heard these things, they held their peace, and glorified God, saying, Then hath God also given unto the Gentiles repentance unto life.

<ns0:div xmlns:ns0="http://www.tei-c.org/ns/1.0" n="10" type="chapter">
               <ns0:head>CHAP. X.</ns0:head>
               <ns0:p>THere was a cert<ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 letter">
                     <ns0:desc>•</ns0:desc>
                  </ns0:gap>in man in <ns0:note n="y" place="bottom">In <ns0:hi>Cesarea Palestine,</ns0:hi> as it was call'd in contra-distincti<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />on to <ns0:hi>Cesarea-Philippi.</ns0:hi>
                  </ns0:note> Cesarea, called <ns0:note n="z" place="bottom">A <ns0:hi>Roman</ns0:hi> by his name; which name was ordinarily to be found amongst the families of the <ns0:hi>Scipio's,</ns0:hi> and <ns0:hi>Sylla's.</ns0:hi>
                  </ns0:note> Cornelius, a centurion of the band <ns0:note n="a" place="bottom">A Band, answers either to a Regiment amongst us, or to a Legion amongst the <ns0:hi>Ro<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />mans</ns0:hi>; (this latter was far greater than the former) It was called the <ns0:hi>Italian</ns0:hi> Band, as being composed of <ns0:hi>Italian</ns0:hi> Sol<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />diers, and might be used as a guard of the Proconsul, who dwelt at <ns0:hi>Cesarea</ns0:hi>; who was that <ns0:hi>Felix</ns0:hi> we read of, <ns0:hi>Chap.</ns0:hi> 23.24.</ns0:note> called the Italian <ns0:hi>band</ns0:hi>
                  <ns0:g ref="char:punc">▪</ns0:g>
               </ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="2">2 <ns0:hi>A</ns0:hi> 
                  <ns0:note n="b" place="bottom">This <ns0:hi>Cornelius</ns0:hi> was a Proselite of the gate, or such as observed the seven precepts of <ns0:hi>Noah</ns0:hi> and lived without giving any offence to the <ns0:hi>Iews.</ns0:hi>
                  </ns0:note> devout <ns0:hi>man,</ns0:hi> and one that feared God <ns0:note n="c" place="bottom">It was a very good sign that he feared God, in that he ingaged all his house to do the like, at least outwardly, which was as much as he could do; this was spoken by God in <ns0:hi>Abrahams</ns0:hi> commendation, <ns0:hi>Gen.</ns0:hi> 18.19.</ns0:note> with all his house, which gave much alms to the people, and prayed to God <ns0:note n="d" place="bottom">He did not neglect the seasons of prayer, especially the time of offering the morning and evening Sa<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />crifice; which by prayer they desired to partake the be<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />nefit of, by which Christ our Sacrifice, and his merits were figured unto them; <ns0:hi>Cornelius</ns0:hi> indeed prayed always, or at all times, taking time in a moral sense, for the seasons and opportunities for such a duty; (as we are commanded to give always thanks, <ns0:hi>Eph.</ns0:hi> 5.20) but he could not pray always, or at all times, taking time in a natural sense; for then he must have neglected all other duties; howsoever, his indeavour was to keep his heart always in a praying dis<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />position.</ns0:note> alway.</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="3">3 He saw in a <ns0:note n="e" place="bottom">Not in a dream or rapture, but sensibly and plainly.</ns0:note> vision evidently, about <ns0:note n="f" place="bottom">Their ninth hour, was with us about three a clock in the afternoon, being the ordinary time for the evening Sa<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />crifice; and by consequence their time of prayer, <ns0:hi>Chap.</ns0:hi> 3.1. And this devout man doth not seek Gods face in vain; <ns0:hi>Cor<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />nelius</ns0:hi> had been faithful in a little, and God would give him much, rather than he should want further instruction, who had improved what he had already; God here sends an Angel, and soon after an Apostle unto him.</ns0:note> the ninth hour of the day, an angel of God coming in to him, and saying unto him, Cornelius.</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="4">4 And when he looked on him, he was <ns0:note n="g" place="bottom">The Angel appeared in so great splendor; all admi<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ration hath some fear with it.</ns0:note> afraid, and said <ns0:note n="h" place="bottom">This is equivolent to What wilt thou have me to do? And shews that <ns0:hi>Cornelius</ns0:hi> was prepared to hear the message.</ns0:note>, What is it Lord? And he said unto him, Thy prayers <ns0:note n="i" place="bottom">Prayer and alms are joyned together in our Saviours discourse concerning them, <ns0:hi>Matth.</ns0:hi> 6.1, &c. in the Apostles order about them, 1 <ns0:hi>Cor.</ns0:hi> 16.1. Alms are our Sacrifices now under the Gospel, <ns0:hi>Phil.</ns0:hi> 4.18. <ns0:hi>Hebr.</ns0:hi> 13.16.</ns0:note> and thine alms are come up for a <ns0:note n="k" place="bottom">An allusion to the offering up of incense under the Law; the smoak of the incense did ascend, and so <ns0:hi>David</ns0:hi> desires that his prayers might ascend to Godward, <ns0:hi>Psal.</ns0:hi> 141.2. thus under the Gospel, prayers are resem<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />bled to incense, <ns0:hi>Rev.</ns0:hi> 8.3. That prayers are said to come up for a memorial, is but the pursuance of the same Metaphor; for <ns0:hi>Lev.</ns0:hi> 2.2. the frankincense, <ns0:hi>&c.</ns0:hi> was the memorial there commanded to be burned; and all this onely to represent unto us, how well-pleasing the prayers of his people are unto God through Christ, and that God keeps in remembrance all those things they thus desire of him, and in his time and measure (which are the best cir<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />cumstances, bestowes all upon them; but let not prayers and alms, which God here hath put together, be put asun<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />der, and in due time we shall reap.</ns0:note> memorial before God.</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="5">
                  <ns0:pb facs="tcp:64193:385" />5 And now send men to <ns0:note n="l" place="bottom">A Town that was memorable for <ns0:hi>Ionahs</ns0:hi> taking ship<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ping there, when he would flee from God, and decline his message, <ns0:hi>Ionah</ns0:hi> 1.3.</ns0:note> Joppa, and call for <ns0:hi>one</ns0:hi> 
                  <ns0:note n="m" place="bottom">The Angel could have declared the Gospel, and instructed <ns0:hi>Cornelius</ns0:hi>; but he sends him to <ns0:hi>Peter,</ns0:hi> God being willing for to honour the means of his own institution.</ns0:note> Simon, whose surname is Peter:</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="6">6 He lodgeth with one <ns0:note n="n" place="bottom">These particulars, when found true by <ns0:hi>Cornelius,</ns0:hi> did very much advantage him towards his believing what <ns0:hi>Peter</ns0:hi> in the name of the Lord did tell him.</ns0:note> Simon a tanner, whose house is by the sea-side: He shall tell thee what thou oughtest to do.</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="7">7 And when the angel which spake unto Corne<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />lius<ns0:g ref="char:punc">▪</ns0:g> was departed, he called two of his <ns0:note n="o" place="bottom">These Servants doubtless <ns0:hi>Cornelius</ns0:hi> had instructed, as ap<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />pears <ns0:hi>ver.</ns0:hi> 2. and God blesses him with faithful and successful service from them.</ns0:note> houshold-servants, and a <ns0:note n="p" place="bottom">No condition, or temptation, too hard for the grace of God to overcome; both Centurion and Soldier, are willing to hazard all they had, rather than not to obey God, and come to the knowledge of Jesus Christ.</ns0:note> devout souldier of them that <ns0:note n="q" place="bottom">This Soldier for his Religion's sake, and his holy life, was taken into nearer attendance on <ns0:hi>Cornelius</ns0:hi>; 'tis no small matter to have one near us, that hath power with God.</ns0:note> waited on him continually.</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="8">8 And <ns0:note n="r" place="bottom">Thus on <ns0:hi>Cornelius</ns0:hi>'s side, all things are disposed to<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />wards his receiving of the Gospel; and the same provi<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />dence at the same time, disposes all things on <ns0:hi>Peters</ns0:hi> part towards his coming to publish it: for</ns0:note> when he had declared all <ns0:hi>these</ns0:hi> things unto them, he sent them to Joppa.</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="9">9 ¶ On the morrow as they went on their journey, and drew nigh unto the city, Peter went up <ns0:note n="s" place="bottom">These houses were flat on the tops, and therefore they were commanded to make battlements for them, <ns0:hi>Deut.</ns0:hi> 22.8. <ns0:hi>Peter</ns0:hi> went on the house-top to pray, that he might from thence view the Temple, which was a type of Christ, through whom onely, we and our prayers can be accepta<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ble unto God; hence 1 <ns0:hi>Kings</ns0:hi> 8.30, &c. there is so often men<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />tion made of praying towards the City, and towards the place which God should chuse; this <ns0:hi>Daniel</ns0:hi> practised, tho upon the hazard of his life, when both City and Tem<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ple were ruined, <ns0:hi>Dan.</ns0:hi> 6.10.</ns0:note> upon the house-top to pray, about the <ns0:note n="t" place="bottom">The sixth hour with them is high-noon, or mid-day, and is accounted one of the three times of prayer, (see <ns0:hi>Chap.</ns0:hi> 3.1.) and was as the <ns0:hi>Iews</ns0:hi> say, recommended to them by <ns0:hi>Isaac</ns0:hi>; howsoever it was the time when they might begin to prepare the evening-Sa<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />crifice; none of these causes need to be assigned, for doubt<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />less this blessed Apostle did watch unto prayer, 1 <ns0:hi>Pet.</ns0:hi> 4.7. and desirously laid hold upon all opportunities to pour out his Soul unto God.</ns0:note> sixth hour.</ns0:p>

Eph. 3.6.</ns0:note>: but<ns0:g ref="char:punc">▪</ns0:g> God hath shewed me, that I should not call any man common or <ns0:note n="k" place="bottom">No man is now unclean by any cere<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />monial uncleanness, because he is not circumcised, or be<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />cause he is not sprinkled with the blood of bulls, <ns0:hi>Hebr.</ns0:hi> 9.13. yet sin hath defiled the whole mass of man kind, and they are equally by nature morally unclean.</ns0:note> unclean.</ns0:p>

God is said to create peace to him that is afar off; <ns0:hi>the Gentile,</ns0:hi> as well as to him that is near, <ns0:hi>the Iew, Psal.</ns0:hi> 72.7, 8. <ns0:hi>Isaiah</ns0:hi> 49.6. and that Salvation was not limited to the <ns0:hi>Iews</ns0:hi> onely, might be known unto them by the e<ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="2 letters">

               <ns0:p n="37">37 <ns0:note n="f" place="bottom">They had heard of the Doctrine of the Gospel by com<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />mon fame and report, (which could not but spread abroad) all might know that Christ and his Apostles did Preach, tho these might be ignorant of the particular Doctrines which they taught, and which <ns0:hi>Peter</ns0:hi> was now sent to in<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />struct them in; or by <ns0:hi>the word,</ns0:hi> (in an usual hebraism) the matter of the Gospel may be meaned, as the Life, Death, and Resurrection of our blessed Saviour, which they could not but have heard several reports of:</ns0:note> The word <ns0:hi>I say</ns0:hi> you know, which was published throughout all Judea, and <ns0:note n="*" place="margin">Luke 4.14.</ns0:note> began from Galilee <ns0:note n="g" place="bottom">Who, as the <ns0:hi>Eli<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />jah</ns0:hi> which was promised, <ns0:hi>Malachi</ns0:hi> 4.5. was the forerunner of the Lord.</ns0:note>, after the baptism which John preached.</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="38">38 How God <ns0:note n="k" place="bottom">It was usual to anoint their Kings, Priests, and Pro<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />phets, unto all which Offices Christ was anointed by his Father; hence called Christ, as in the Old Testament the Messiah.</ns0:note> anointed Jesus <ns0:note n="i" place="bottom">The Apostle is not ashamed of this name, tho given to our Saviour by way of contempt; he gloried in the cross of Christ.</ns0:note> of Nazareth with <ns0:note n="k" place="bottom">Christ was indued with the Almighty Spirit of God, and with the power of it.</ns0:note> the holy Ghost, and with power, who went about <ns0:note n="l" place="bottom">All the miracles our blessed Saviour wrought, were works of mercy, for the benefit and relief of those upon whom he wrought them; he could have wrought miracles to destroy and ruine such as would not believe in him, which he was often provoked unto; (nay, his Apostles would have had him but to permit them by fire from Heaven to destroy the <ns0:hi>Samaritans, Luke</ns0:hi> 9.54. and he would no<ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 letter">

               <ns0:p n="40">40 Him <ns0:note n="q" place="bottom">Lest these <ns0:hi>Gentiles</ns0:hi> be deterred from believing in Christ, and take offence at his Cross: St. <ns0:hi>Peter</ns0:hi> Preached unto them the Resurrection, which suddenly and powerfully fol<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />lowed.</ns0:note> God raised up the third day, and <ns0:note n="r" place="bottom">And this he tells them was unquestionable, as appeared by all the ways that any thing can be proved by; Christ was seen, and heard, and felt after his Resurrection, as the beloved Disciple tells us, 1 <ns0:hi>Iohn</ns0:hi> 1.1. and manifested his victory over death for us.</ns0:note> shewed him openly.</ns0:p>

Micah 7.18.</ns0:note> To him <ns0:note n="a" place="bottom">This our Saviour had told his Apostles, which St. <ns0:hi>Peter</ns0:hi> here Preaches to his Auditors: It was included in the very first promise recorded by <ns0:hi>Moses, Gen.</ns0:hi> 3.15. <ns0:hi>The seed of the woman shall break the serpents head</ns0:hi>; and so continued through all ages of the Church, to be ma<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />nifest in such degrees as it pleased the wisdm of God to make it known; 'tis certain that all the ceremonial Law concerning Sacrifices, did testifie this very thing; for by it, it did appear, that without shedding of blood there was no remission of sin, as <ns0:hi>Heb.</ns0:hi> 9.22. and 'tis manifest by the light of nature, that the blood of <ns0:hi>bulls and goats, could not take away sins,</ns0:hi> as Heb. 10.4.</ns0:note> give all the Prophets witness, that through <ns0:hi>b</ns0:hi> his name whosoever believeth in him, shall receive remission of sins.<ns0:note n="c" place="bottom">But through Christs name, for his sake, and by vertue of his merit, who died <ns0:hi>for our sins, and rose again for our Iustification,</ns0:hi> Rom. 4.25. <ns0:hi>We shall receive remission of sins,</ns0:hi> Heb. 9.13, 14.</ns0:note>

               <ns0:p n="45">45 And <ns0:note n="e" place="bottom">Such as were not onely themselves circumcised, but born of circumcised parents, who are thus called, <ns0:hi>Gal.</ns0:hi> 2.12.</ns0:note> they of the circumcision which belie<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ved, were astonished, as many as came with Peter, because <ns0:note n="f" place="bottom">These not minding<ns0:g ref="char:punc">▪</ns0:g> or understanding the many predicti<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ons of the calling of the <ns0:hi>Gentiles,</ns0:hi> thought that Christ was onely promised unto the <ns0:hi>Iews</ns0:hi>; and were amazed to see now such an Argument as might convince them to the con<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />trary.</ns0:note> that on the Gentiles also was poured out the gift of the holy Ghost.<ns0:note n="g" place="bottom">Pouring out, speaks the abundant measure in which the Holy Ghost was given unto them.</ns0:note>
